present.E_AGENT: the Bute estate agent, Cardiff (an office, not a named person)

logline: In the Bute estate office the agent prepares a notice to quit for Great House Farm, Llandough. This is the 1877 step that Mary (Nancy) Williams's later account reports.

moment.summary: In the Bute estate office the agent prepares a notice to quit for Great House Farm, Llandough. This is the 1877 step that Mary (Nancy) Williams's later account reports.
captions: 1877: Mary (Nancy) Williams's later account reports a sale of the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas, with about 9 acres kept by Bute. The deed and plan are missing (CH-0025)
1877: A Bute–Daniel Thomas & Son agreement (sale or quarry lease) is known only from a family plan image and family account. The deed is not held (EV-0006)
1877: The Bute trustees' abstract of receipts and payments (Bute X.6(12)) is not yet obtained. It may show a sale price or only rent (EV-0007)

6 Nov 1877: Mary (Nancy) Williams's account gives this date for a lease to John Williams. No matching Llandough deed has been found. The Bute lease of this date to John Williams, builder, is for Clyde Street, Roath, not the farm (CH-0026)
6 Nov 1877: Reported lease to John Williams. The original is not located; parties, land, plan, rent and term are unknown (EV-0008)
moment.basis: This rests only on Mary (Nancy) Williams's c.1974 statement. No notice, deed or plan is held. The estate-office moment is the most likely way such a notice was made, and no Williams is shown.

subtitles: en/es subtitles for Welsh speech; Rioplatense Spanish; cues <=2x42 chars
accent: thick Welsh accent for every Welsh character; non-Welsh characters keep their own accents
continuity: The folded notice waits in the tray; cut to Llandough, where the census enumerator calls at the farm to collect John Williams's household schedule.
